newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Provisional financing figures for March 1997.
newsitem.headline: Provisional financing figures for March 1997.

text.p: Financing of 2,466.2 million rand was obtained in government bonds while net short-term loans decreased by 470.4 million rand during March this year, South Africa's Finance Department said on Wednesday.

To finance the first repayment of the Compensatory and Contingency Financing Facility of the International Monetary Fund 345.3 million rand was transferred from the IMF Deposit Account at the South African Reserve Bank, which brings the total financing for the month to 2,341.1 million rand.

The Finance Department said in a statement the provisional figures indicated that financing of the 1996/97 budget had exceeded the revised estimates published in the 1997 Budget Review by 2,018 million rand, mainly as a result of the additional issuance of government bonds during March 1997.

Additional borrowing during March was undertaken in order to meet end of year expenditure commitments, to provide for balances to be carried to 1997/98 and to allow for possible lags in revenue receipts as a result of the long weekend coinciding with the fiscal year end, the department said.
Government bonds and debentures to the amount of 16,648 million rand and foreign loans to the amount of 1,899 million rand were redeemed during April 1996 to March 1997.
